title: Machine learning and synthesis clarify metastable phases of carbon
summary: An algorithm constructed metastable phase diagrams of carbon and identified structural features of n-diamond that were then verified experimentally. The group also synthesized predicted phases and compared structures under a microscope; the work concerns carbon only and does not establish useful properties of the new materials.

evidence.tested: Workflow found 505 candidate carbon structures; a neural network trained on 273 phases, test error 37.1 meV/atom. Diamond-anvil laser-heating experiments on graphite with electron microscopy were used to compare predicted metastable phases, including n-diamond.
evidence.unknown: The search is not guaranteed exhaustive; the paper calls cubic-diaphite a candidate structure for n-diamond. The model had higher errors at high pressure; kinetics are only partly covered. Argonne synthesis of unreported phases was not seen in the paper text read.
evidence.ai_role: A deep neural network predicted Gibbs free energy; a support vector machine drew phase boundaries; an evolutionary search proposed structures. Humans ran the experiments.
